name: Nutrien Ltd.
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat: irreplaceable low-cost Saskatchewan potash mines with long-life reserves, North American low-cost nitrogen (cheap gas feedstock), scale as the world's largest fertilizer producer, and the largest ag-retail distribution network give a real cost and distribution advantage — but Nutrien is fundamentally a commodity price-taker in potash/nitrogen/phosphate, earnings swing with global fertilizer benchmarks it does not control, and returns collapse in down-cycles (OE/share $10.73 in 2022 to $2.98 in 2024), so pricing power is not proven through a cycle.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 3.4%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 40-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Nutrien Form F-10 prospectus filed 2026-03-31 (and 40-F annual filing, CIK 1725964): 'Our Common Shares are listed on the TSX and on the NYSE under the symbol NTR' — the NYSE security is the common share itself, directly listed, not an ADS; system README v5.3 note also lists NTR among direct-listed ordinary shares at ratio 1.0) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.1x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 4.7x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Real low-cost potash/retail franchise, moat 5/10, but a cyclical commodity price-taker with 4.7x net debt/OE — at $70.49 it does not clear 15%: weighted IRR 8.1%, weighted IV@15% $31.77; clears 15% only below ~$31.77.
moat_for: Low-cost, long-life Saskatchewan potash mines — among the world's largest reserves, not replicable on any investable timeline
Scale: world's largest fertilizer company and largest crop-input retailer, with purchasing and logistics advantages
Low-cost North American nitrogen plants on cheap natural gas feedstock; H1 2026 controllable potash cash cost below $60/tonne
Retail distribution network provides a steadier, service/proprietary-products margin stream that dampens pure commodity exposure
moat_against: Commodity price-taker: potash/nitrogen/phosphate prices are set globally; Nutrien does not control its main earnings driver
Cyclicality proven in its own history: OE/share spanned $10.73 (2022) to $2.98 (2024), revenue 3-yr CAGR -10.8%
New global potash supply (e.g. BHP Jansen) and Russian/Belarusian supply normalization can pressure prices and volumes
Capital-intensive mining/chemical assets: capex ~$1.9-2.4B/yr and net debt 4.7x normalized OE leave little buffer in a down-cycle
Retail is a low-margin distribution business exposed to farm incomes, weather, and acreage
